cards.back: Alcohol and drugs impair driving, making it very hard or impossible to drive safely, and drunk or drugged driving threatens everyone on the road.
cards.front: How do alcohol and drugs affect your ability to drive?

cards.back: Blood alcohol concentration, or BAC, measures how much alcohol is in your blood.
cards.front: What does BAC measure?

cards.back: You cannot judge your BAC by counting drinks, because weight, body fat, and when and how much you ate change how your body handles alcohol.
cards.front: Why can you not judge your BAC by counting drinks?

cards.back: Fatigue, mood and medications also change how alcohol affects your driving.
cards.front: Besides food and weight, what else changes how alcohol affects your driving?

cards.back: Safe driving needs constant awareness of the vehicles in front of, behind and beside you.
cards.front: Where should you stay aware of other vehicles?

decks.module: why BAC is hard to judge and staying aware

cards.back: Maryland treats a driver as under the influence of alcohol at a BAC of point zero eight or above.
cards.front: At what BAC does Maryland treat a driver as under the influence?
cards.memory_hook: Point zero eight is the line

cards.back: Any amount of alcohol can hurt your driving: judgment and coordination may suffer well below point zero eight, which can still lead to criminal charges.
cards.front: Can you be charged with an alcohol-related offense below point zero eight?

cards.back: Even one drink can affect your vision, simple movements and reaction time and raise your crash risk.
cards.front: How many drinks can affect your vision and reaction time?

cards.back: Drinking any alcohol at all is illegal for anyone under twenty-one.
cards.front: How much alcohol may a person under twenty-one legally drink?

cards.back: A driver under twenty-one who is stopped after drinking will have the license suspended or revoked and may also be charged with breaking the license's alcohol restriction.
cards.front: What happens to a driver under twenty-one stopped after drinking?

cards.back: Driving with an open alcohol container in the passenger area of the vehicle is against the law.
cards.front: Where in the vehicle is an open alcohol container against the law?

cards.back: An open container is any opened can, bottle, container or package, and a six-pack with open, empty or missing cans or bottles can count as one.
cards.front: Can a six-pack with a missing can count as an open container?

cards.back: The passenger area covers the driver and passenger seats and any spot the driver or passengers can easily reach while seated.
cards.front: What does the passenger area include?

cards.back: The legal under-the-influence line is a BAC of point zero eight, but impairment and criminal charges are possible at lower levels, and drivers under twenty-one may not drink any alcohol.
cards.front: Besides the point zero eight line, what other alcohol rules apply?

cards.back: The open-container ban is tied to the passenger area, and that area is defined as the seats plus anywhere occupants can easily reach while sitting, not just the seats themselves.
cards.front: Is the open-container passenger area just the seats?

decks.module: the BAC limit and impairment below it; zero alcohol under twenty-one; open containers and the passenger area

cards.back: Illegal drugs, some prescription medicines and chemical inhalants can badly affect alertness, concentration, coordination and reaction time.
cards.front: Which of these can badly affect alertness and reaction time?

cards.back: All drugs can make it harder to judge distance and to respond to signals and sounds on the road.
cards.front: What can all drugs make harder on the road?

cards.back: Driving under the influence of controlled dangerous substances can get your license suspended or revoked.
cards.front: What can happen to your license for driving under the influence of controlled dangerous substances?

cards.back: Read prescription and over-the-counter labels for warnings against driving or running heavy machinery; driving impaired against such a warning can bring a criminal charge.
cards.front: What should you look for on medicine labels?

cards.back: If you are convicted of drunk or drugged driving with a child in the vehicle, the judge may double your fine and jail time.
cards.front: What may a judge do if you are convicted of drunk driving with a child in the vehicle?

decks.module: drugs, medicines and label warnings; doubled penalties with a child aboard

cards.back: Aggressive driving includes speeding, tailgating, ignoring signals and devices, unsafe lane changes, failing to yield and unsafe or illegal passing.
cards.front: Which of these is aggressive driving?

cards.back: Crowded roads, surprise delays, hurrying, construction and stress can push people into driving aggressively.
cards.front: What can push people into driving aggressively?

cards.back: To avoid aggressive-driving incidents, leave extra travel time, stay patient and courteous, and focus on your own driving.
cards.front: How can you avoid aggressive-driving incidents?

cards.back: Other anti-aggression habits are signaling what you plan to do, obeying all traffic controls, yielding the right-of-way and refusing to compete with other drivers.
cards.front: Which habit helps avoid aggressive driving?

cards.back: A useful rule is to treat other drivers and road users the way you want them to treat you.
cards.front: What is a useful general rule for treating other road users?

decks.module: aggressive driving and how to avoid it

cards.back: Distracted driving means taking your eyes, your hands or, above all, your mind off driving.
cards.front: What does distracted driving mean?

cards.back: Distracted driving causes more police-reported crashes than any other cause.
cards.front: What causes more police-reported crashes than anything else?

cards.back: Distractions include eating or drinking, adjusting music or a GPS, handling children or pets, loose objects, phone calls or texting, smoking, makeup, shaving, reading and talking with passengers.
cards.front: Which of these is listed as a driving distraction?

cards.back: Using a hand-held cell phone while driving, texting included, is illegal, so you may not drive while holding your phone.
cards.front: May you drive while holding your cell phone in Maryland?

cards.back: Drivers under eighteen may not use a cell phone at all while driving, even hands-free, except to call nine hundred eleven in an emergency.
cards.front: May a driver under eighteen use a hands-free phone while driving?

cards.back: Drivers eighteen and older may use a phone hands-free, while drivers under eighteen may not use one at all except for a nine hundred eleven call, and no driver may use a hand-held phone.
cards.front: How do phone rules differ for drivers eighteen and older versus under eighteen?

decks.module: distracted driving; hand-held ban and the under-eighteen phone rule

cards.back: Adult drivers may make calls hands-free, but should keep phone use to a minimum.
cards.front: How may adult drivers make calls while driving?

cards.back: Safer phone habits are to call only in emergencies, let a passenger place the call when possible, or pull safely off the road and stop first.
cards.front: What is a safer phone habit if you must make a call?

cards.back: Let voicemail pick up incoming calls and keep any conversation short.
cards.front: How should incoming calls be handled while driving?

cards.back: People who drive many miles daily, people with sleep disorders and people on certain medicines face a higher risk of drowsiness.
cards.front: Who faces a higher risk of drowsiness?

decks.module: safer phone habits and drowsiness risk groups

cards.back: Lack of sleep slows reaction time, lowers awareness and impairs judgment much as drugs or alcohol do, sharply raising crash risk.
cards.front: How does lack of sleep affect driving?

cards.back: Drowsiness warning signs include eyes closing or blurring, trouble holding your head up, nonstop yawning and drifting, disconnected thoughts.
cards.front: Which of these is a drowsiness warning sign?

cards.back: Other drowsiness signs are not recalling the last few miles, missing your exit, repeatedly leaving your lane and repeatedly changing speed.
cards.front: Which of these is another drowsiness sign?

cards.back: If you get tired or sleepy at the wheel, the best response is to rest or switch drivers.
cards.front: What is the best response to feeling sleepy at the wheel?

cards.back: Drowsiness impairs judgment and reaction time much like alcohol, and the cure is rest or a new driver rather than pushing on.
cards.front: What is the cure for drowsy driving?

cards.back: The manual's campaign page states that one-third of fatal crashes are caused by distracted driving, with cell phone use among the leading distractions.
cards.front: According to the campaign page, what share of fatal crashes are caused by distracted driving?

cards.back: Every year tens of thousands of people are arrested on Maryland roads for drunk or drugged driving.
cards.front: How many people are arrested each year on Maryland roads for impaired driving?

cards.back: Before going out, plan a safe way home and name a sober driver, since an impaired-driving arrest brings large fines, possible jail and thousands of dollars in court costs.
cards.front: What should you plan before going out to drink?

decks.module: campaign facts on distraction and impaired-driving arrests
